reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself, since the handoff only comes from W2's summary. I'll start by listing the orders.
The handoff says refunds were applied, but I should verify that against the refunds list before paying anyone. Next I'll list the refunds.
The refunds list matches W2's handoff: orders 140, 144, and 145 each have a refund, and none exceeds its order amount. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
acme's net_balance of 31766 matches the order and refund data I checked. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net_balance of 35795 matches my check: orders 141 and 144 total 55259, minus the 19464 refund on order 144. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

I checked all three net balances against the orders and refunds: acme 45425-13659=31766, birch 55259-19464=35795, cobalt 20917-9501=11416. Each matches, and no refund exceeds its order, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 31766 is recorded. Birch's net of 35795 matches orders 141 and 144 minus the refund on 144, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt is the last customer. Its payout is 11416 per my check (20917 orders minus 9501 refund), so I'll record that payout now.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches the order and refund data I checked. The batch is complete.
